results.occurrenceRemarks: Free-standing Ficus lyrata specimen located in Potts Point, NSW, within a Heritage Conservation Area. The tree is mature, healthy, and structurally stable. It reaches Level 5 of the adjacent residential building, with a broad, dome-shaped crown that spans an estimated 2–3 metres less than the tree’s height. The trunk is well-developed and free of visible defects. The tree exhibits regular fruiting and consistent leaf renewal, with no recent vertical extension, suggesting a stable mature phase. Its foliage is dense and well-distributed throughout the crown. The tree’s size, crown structure, and consistent reproductive behaviour suggest that it has been growing undisturbed at this location for many decades. This observation records a well-established individual of Ficus lyrata growing outside its native tropical range. The species is not listed as invasive in New South Wales.
